newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 30.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849. Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
VOTER TURNOUT MODERATE, POLLS PEACEFUL

Byelections to three parliamentary and nine state assembly constituencies were marked by low voter turnout in some constituencies to fairly brisk in others. In East Delhi parliamentary constituency there was a record low of 23-25 percent voting. The three parliamentary constituencies included Ernakulam in Kerala, Aska in Orissa and east Delhi.
Indian Express
CONGRESS INFIGHTING GOES PUBLIC

Sniping in the Congress party began on the first day of campaigning for the party president's election. Sharad Pawar accused party chief Sitaram Kesri of malpractices but the party chief rejected them outright.
The Times Of India
PAWAR WANTS SONIA GANDHI TO HEAD PARTY

Congress party leader Sharad Pawar indicated he would withdraw from the contest for the post of party president if party chief Sitaram Kesri was willing to follow suit in favour of Sonia Gandhi, the widow of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi.
The Economic Times
NORMS FOR INVESTING ABROAD EASED

The government has decided to allow corporates to freely invest overseas up to $15 million raised through export earnings or global depositary receipts (GDRs) without taking permission either from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) or the finance ministry.
BANKS, FINANCIAL FIRMS RESIST DECLINE IN COUPON RATES

Banks and institutional investors are resisting the continued hammering down of coupon rates by corporate debt issuers. These bulk investors are reluctant to touch paper with interest rates lower than their own prime lending rate (PLR). While the PLR of most banks is at 14.5 to 15 percent, that of financial institutions stand at 15 percent. The first signs of resistance are already apparent in the case of the 10-billion rupee Industrial Development Bank of India's (IDBI) offer of bonds at 13.55 percent. Other players trying to place debts at rates of 13.75 to 14.25 percent is also a cause of concern, merchant bank sources said.
DEPOSITS OF 350,000 RUPEES AND ABOVE TO BE VERIFIED

The draft of a law to check money laundering to be introduced for passage in the monsoon session of parliament will seek to verify the antecedents of all bank deposits of 350,000 rupees and above. The Act will have stringent provisions. Banks will have to mandatorily the source of all deposits amounting to this amount and above.
Financial Express
NSE SLASHES TRADING CHARGES FOR DEMAT SEGMENT

The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has slashed transaction charges for trading in the dematerialised segment by nearly 50 percent. A transaction on the dematerialised segment will now carry a charge of only 0.005 percent as against the earlier 0.009 percent. The NSE has decided to introduce the charges with retrospective effect. The new charges will be applicable from April 2. The move is expected to provide a major thrust to the depository as it will provide the much-needed incentive to investors to settle their trades through the dematerialised mode.
CORP BANK'S 2.66 BLN RUPEE ISSUE LIKELY IN SEPTEMBER
The Corporation Bank plans to enter the capital market with a 2.66 billion rupee public issue in September this year. The 10-rupee shares will carry a premium of at least 60 rupees.
Business Standard
FOREIGN INVESTORS PREFER GDRS TO BOURSE

Foreign investors are finding inefficiencies in the Indian stock market and are preferring to buy Indian global depository receipts (GDRs) to direct purchases on domestic bourses, says a World Bank report. Foreign participants cite inefficiencies in clearance, settlement and depository systems in domestic stock exchanges as reasons for their interest in Indian GDRs.
RESERVE BANK PROPOSES ETHICS CODE FOR FINANCE COMPANIES

The Reserve Bank (RBI) has asked non-banking finance companies and their associations to work out a code of conduct for themselves and evolve self-regulatory measures. It has also asked these associations to set up customer grievances cells and educate the depositors about the risk elements involved.
CUT IN LETTER OF INTENT PERIOD FOR SUGAR UNITS

In a move to curb pre-emptive licences that block out new competitors, the government reduced the validity of letters of intent (LoI) offering licences for new sugar units to one year from three years. The new norms are meant to ensure that licensed capacity is created according to schedule to guard the interests of farmers, the industry and the consumers.
WORLD BANK PRESCRIBES A BITTER PILL FOR INDUSTRY

The World Bank has suggested reforms in the sugar industry over the next two or three years. These include elimination of all entry barriers, phasing out of compulsory state purchase quotas for sugar and the setting up of a new body to supervise sugarcane pricing.
The Observer
PRIME MINISTER CONSIDERING OPTIONS FOR FUEL PRICE HIKE

Indicating another round of hike in petroleum goods, Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said the government was examining a fuel price hike to bridge a huge deficit, but added that a final decision would taketime as it required a political consensus with coalition partners.
GOVERNMENT ALLOWS FREE IMPORT OF RICE

The government removed restrictions on the import of common/coarse rice and, rice with 50 percent or more broken. The move is aimed at increasing the availability of common/coarse variety rice and to check the increasing prices of some coarse varieties of rice.
RESERVE BANK WELCOMES PRIVATE BANKERS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has welcomed private bankers to set up banks with smaller capital as per guidelines announced earlier to serve local investors. The RBI governor said individuals or groups of people willing to establish private banks and local area banks with smaller capital are welcome, provided they meet the required rules.
